about: The behaviour every implementation of the migration runner must show
(db/README.md, "Running the migrations"). Both runners iterate this file:
A case runs its steps in order against one fresh, empty database.
Each step runs the runner over `dir`, relative to db/conformance, and then
checks the state the step describes:
expect            'ok', or the error code the run must raise
applied           how many rows this step added to public.schema_migrations
(optional; a step that raises may still have applied files)
applied_versions  public.schema_migrations after the step, ascending;
tables_exist      schema-qualified relations that must exist afterwards
tables_absent     schema-qualified relations that must not exist

cases.name: basic
cases.description: Two files apply in ascending order on an empty database.

cases.name: rerun
cases.description: Running the same directory twice applies nothing the second time. Both fixture files insert a row, so a re-application would fail on the primary key instead of reporting ok.

cases.name: hash_change
cases.description: An applied file whose bytes changed stops the run before anything else is applied. The variant differs from the applied 0001 by one character of a comment.

cases.name: failing
cases.description: A file that raises halfway is rolled back whole: the table it created first is gone and no row records it.

cases.name: out_of_order
cases.description: A file numbered below an applied version is refused; the gap is filled with a new higher number instead.

cases.name: missing_file
cases.description: An applied version with no file on disk is refused: the directory no longer describes the database.

cases.name: bad_filename
cases.description: One file that does not match NNNN_slug.sql refuses the whole directory, before the well-named file beside it is applied.
